sources.title: VENTURE experiment: exploratory notes on abandoned-plugin demand
sources.excerpt: People keep picking the abandoned plugin because it is known and ranks well, not because nothing else exists.

evidence.claim: 158 of 2,151 popular WordPress plugins (7.3%) have gone two years without an update while keeping at least 10,000 installs, and all of them are still downloaded hundreds of times a month.
evidence.quote: Orphaned (not updated for 24 months, ≥ 10,000 installs): 158 (7.3% of plugins with that many installs).

evidence.claim: Of the 10 most-downloaded abandoned plugins, 9 already have a maintained alternative that does the same job. The tenth is a hosting provider's own plugin that no one else could replace.
evidence.quote: Unserved: 1 of 10, and that one (#7) is a hosting provider's own plugin that no third party could replace.

evidence.claim: Users stay on abandoned plugins because they're known and rank well, not because alternatives are missing: the gap is discovery and migration, not an empty niche.
evidence.quote: People keep picking the abandoned plugin because it is known and ranks well, not because nothing else exists.
evidence.context: Exploratory; based on one striking case (Transients Manager) and the general pattern.
